## Clinical background

Transplantation is now standard care for people with HIV and end-stage kidney or liver disease, but there is less evidence for pancreas transplantation [@blumberg2019astid]. A national registry study of pancreas transplants from 2001 to 2021 found similar pancreas graft and patient survival in recipients with and without HIV [@bharadwaj2024pancreas]. The [clinical background](quarto/background.qmd) page gives more detail.

## What this analysis does

This analysis compares outcomes after kidney–pancreas and pancreas-alone transplantation between recipients with and without HIV in the United States. It uses the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) standard analysis files, which cover every transplant performed in the country.

[Braces](https://forum.posit.co/t/curly-braces-around-package-name-convention/122547) identify R packages throughout this site.

## Methods

Recipients with HIV are compared with similar recipients without HIV of the same transplant type in two ways: by matching each to up to ten recipients without HIV, and by weighting all recipients without HIV to resemble those with HIV. Graft loss, rejection, death and cancer after transplant are then compared. [Study design and methods](quarto/study_methods.qmd) explains each step in plain language, and the authoritative specification is the [analysis plan](quarto/analysis-plan.qmd).

## Status

Preliminary. The analysis plan is a draft with several decisions still open, and a draft of the code exists but has not yet been run on SRTR data. This site shows the shared setup and helper code; pages for the analysis steps are added as each step is settled. No results are shown. Open decisions are tracked in the project's [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/HIV-pancreas-2024-srtr/issues).
